blind_projection.competing_explanation: Matched against the frozen BPR_MF control; any gain must come from the added residual-memory gate rather than from data, split, or optimization differences.
expected_evidence: If the gate does not consistently alter ranking quality across seeds, the hypothesis is weakened.
Mechanism-on vs mechanism-off comparison under the same frozen split shows a stable NDCG@10 difference.
Removing the residual-memory gate collapses the lift toward the BPR_MF baseline.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the wrapped model does not outperform the matched control when the gate is enabled, or if turning the gate off leaves performance essentially unchanged, the hypothesis is false.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: The change adds a new user-conditioned residual representation and an explicit on/off interaction path, which alters core representation and interaction structure rather than only adjusting regularization or hyperparameters.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A BPR-MF recommender augmented with a short-history user residual memory and a gate that interpolates between direct affinity and residual intent will improve frozen-split full-sort NDCG@10 because it separates stable compatibility from context-local preference corrections; this improvement should vanish when the residual path is disabled.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same BPR_MF backbone, embedding budget, negative sampling, optimizer, and training schedule; vary only the residual-memory gate and its mechanism-off ablation.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Wrap BPR_MF with a user-conditioned residual intent memory computed from recent positive interactions, then score candidates by gated interpolation between direct user-item affinity and residual-transported affinity; include a hard mechanism-off branch that disables the residual path.
